messages:
sarah: noticed spike in errors during the v2 gradual rollout — error rate from 0.6% -> 3.4% at ~6k qps, started at 17:02 UTC. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.example/reports/rollout-v2 :rotating_light:
incident-bot: AUTO-INCIDENT created (sev=P1) — paging @maria. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-2026-0423-7
maria: oncall here, looking. thanks for the flag. can someone pause traffic to the canary while we triage? prefer stop rollout rather than force rollback until we confirm impact. tagging @eli and @tom to help root cause.
sarah: pausing now — updating rollout policy to 0% for canary cohort. command run: ```redwood rollout update --id canary-v2 --target-percent 0 --actor=sarah```
deploy-bot: rollout update accepted — canary-v2 target-percent=0 queued (job id: jb-8245). will drain in ~15s and stop new canary assignments.
eli: seeing error spikes correlated with sequence-len > 1024, memory growth on gpu nodes for serving-v2-quantized. past 10mins logs: ```[2026-04-23T17:02:35Z] model_server.py ERROR OOM on batch 17 size 48
[2026-04-23T17:02:37Z] backend-kvcache WARN corrupted prefix cache entry for conn 12```
tom: confirmed increased tail latency on generation endpoints (p99 jump 950ms -> 3.2s). ingest path seems healthy, issue appears in model runtime stage. I recommend immediate rollback to stable image while we debug quantization path.
maria: agreed. initiating manual rollback to stable-20260410. I'll run the rollback job and pin to stable. command: ```redwood deploy rollback --deployment canary-v2 --to stable-20260410 --force-traffic=true --actor=maria```
deploy-bot: rollback job started (rb-9221). pulling image stable-20260410 -> initiating evict + replace on 4 canary instances. logs: ```rb-9221: stage=pull image=stable-20260410
rb-9221: stage=evict old=canary-v2 inst=vm-prod-17
rb-9221: stage=replace inst=vm-prod-17 status=ok
rb-9221: stage=complete elapsed=38s```
elI: running smoke and synthetic tests against stable after traffic shift. smoke script: ```for u in 1 2 3; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}' | jq -r '.ok'; done``` results: ok, ok, ok. p95 latency back to ~420ms.
pj: checking customer-facing errors — Sentry shows ~40 distinct user errors during canary window, primarily from generated-text truncation and timeout exceptions. PR status: created issue INC-2026-0423-7 in tracker and added stack traces.
customer-ops: status page updated: "Investigating elevated errors for some text-generation requests. Rolling back recent canary to stable version while we validate." sent to customers via status.redwood.example and to top-10 customers impacted.
maria: switching severity to mitigated since rollback finished and synthetic checks look green. leaving open for follow-up and root cause. assigning to eli for next shift.
eli: taking post-rollback ownership. next steps: collect full heapdumps from failed nodes, run reproducer with seq-len >1024, bisect quantization flag changes between stable and canary images. I'll schedule a debug window @ 20:00 UTC.
sarah: timeline note: 17:02 alert, 17:03 rollout paused, 17:05 rollback triggered, 17:06 rollback complete, 17:10 smoke tests green. impacted customer messages sent at 17:15.
maria: handoff: i'm leaving notes in the incident doc and will follow up in postmortem. @eli, if you need extra infra quota ping me. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED — severity set to mitigated by maria. next: postmortem-assignee=eli; statuspage=updated; oncall_handoff=true.
pj: quick note — recommend adding a pre-rolling test for sequences >1024 in the deploy pipeline and gating the quantization flag behind a canary-specific runtime safety net.
maria: agreed, will add blocked PR checklist and a temporary rollout guard rule (fail fast if OOM seen N times in X minutes).
customer-ops: creating customer follow-up message template for those who reported timeouts, will include cause and mitigation steps, and offer 1:1 support.
maria: closing on-call handoff. if anything new surfaces, reopen thread or call pager. thanks all. :pray:
